findings.reason: the section already had four attempts churning request plumbing; naming the owning mechanism in the design text is what stops a fifth parallel implementation.
findings.text: §3's design text proposes "one lax state machine whose sole operator body serves residual, merit, acceptance, recovery, reconciliation and Jacobian-vector requests" without naming that this machine already exists at fixed_point.py:923-1055, so a node dispatched to §3 can build a parallel request enum and body instead of extending the committed one

findings.reason: the section should name cache_reuse_summary.py as the key enumerator and have the guard reuse or extend its convention, rather than defining program-key membership a second time.
findings.text: §4 asks the guard's `served_entries` to count program-key cache entries, but the cache-key enumeration and its on-disk filename convention are already owned by `scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_reuse_summary.py` (`pin_programs`, `prewarm_programs`, `served_keys`), so a second, differently-defined key count in cache_guard drifts from that owner

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the machinery the plan extends is one deep module (a request kind plus payload reaching a single shared operator body); §2 adds gates and §4 edits two guard functions, neither of which spreads complexity across new shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 introduces a second "program-key entry" count inside `cache_guard.py` when `cache_reuse_summary.py` already owns the cache-key enumeration and its filename convention.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section adds to any family, so nothing needs naming as retired or merged.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3's design subsection describes building "one lax state machine" as if new, and never cites `nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py:923-1055` (`OperatorRequestKind`/`operator_request_body/`run_operator_requests`), which already is that machine.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan edits the existing owner in place (`cache_guard.py` `served_entries`, the fixed_point request bodies) rather than putting a new thin layer over machinery it leaves untouched.
